# ACN (Accenture plc) — Technical Analysis Report
**Analysis date: 2026-10-01 | Verified close: 212.30 | Verified range: 211.04 – 227.63 (open 215.98) on 28.98M volume**

## Indicator selection rationale
The selected set covers trend (close_50_sma, close_200_sma, close_10_ema), momentum (macd, rsi), volatility/breakout context (boll_ub, boll_lb, atr). Together they capture complementary signals without redundancy: moving averages frame the trend regime, MACD/RSI quantify momentum, Bollinger bands locate the price within its volatility envelope, and ATR calibrates risk sizing.

## Key observation: an extreme gap day on 2026-10-01
The verified snapshot shows ACN closed 2026-09-30 at 183.37 and opened 2026-10-01 at 215.98 — an overnight gap of roughly +17.8% — trading as high as 227.63 before fading to close at 212.30. Volume was 28.98M, roughly 4–6x the typical ~4–10M daily volume seen through August–September. This is a news/event-driven repricing (e.g., earnings-style gap), not a gradual trend move. Intraday character matters: the close at 212.30 sits below the open (215.98) and well off the 227.63 high — a bearish intraday candle despite the massive gain, indicating supply absorption at higher levels.

## Trend structure
- **Close (212.30) vs 50 SMA (178.89):** Price is ~18.7% above the 50-day average, which was still rising (175.33 → 178.89 over the last week). Prior to the gap, ACN was in a corrective phase: after peaking near 195 on 09-14, price slid to a 174.47 low on 09-28, below the then-flattening short-term averages.
- **Close (212.30) vs 200 SMA (193.81):** Price has reclaimed the long-term benchmark decisively — it had been trading below a declining 200 SMA (still falling from ~200.7 on 09-01 to 193.81) for the entire look-back window. The gap catapulted ACN from ~5.4% below the 200 SMA to ~9.5% above it in one session.
- **50 SMA (178.89) vs 200 SMA (193.81):** The death-cross configuration persists — the medium-term trend remains below the long-term trend — but the gap dramatically narrows the gap. If price holds above ~194, a golden-cross setup becomes a real medium-term possibility, though the 200 SMA is still declining.

## Momentum
- **RSI jumped to 70.01** from 52.32 the prior day — a one-day swing from neutral to the overbought threshold. This reflects the gap magnitude rather than sustained momentum; RSI this extreme after a single-session repricing frequently precedes either consolidation or partial retracement ("gap fill" risk toward the ~183–195 zone).
- **MACD flipped positive to 2.57** (signal 1.81, histogram +0.76) after hovering near zero / negative through late September (−0.08 on 09-29, +0.11 on 09-30). This is a fresh bullish crossover, but it is entirely driven by one bar — the MACD had been deteriorating steadily from ~7.7 at the start of September, and a single gap can produce a whipsaw crossover that fails if follow-through doesn't materialize.

## Volatility and positioning within the bands
- **ATR spiked to 9.58** from a stable ~6.8–7.4 regime — a ~38% jump. Risk sizing assumptions from September are stale; stops and position sizes need recalibration for the new volatility regime.
- **Close (212.30) is above the upper Bollinger band (203.00)**, with the band itself blowing out from ~196.5 to 203.0 in one day and the lower band dropping to 167.02. Band expansion on a close above the upper band signals a volatility breakout, but closes this far outside the band are statistically prone to mean reversion toward the middle band (185.01) in the near term.

## Actionable insights
- **Chasing risk is elevated.** Buying at 212+ means paying above the upper band with RSI at the overbought line, against an intraday pattern (open > close, close near the low end of a 16.6-point range) that shows sellers active into strength. Patient entries on a pullback toward the 200–203 zone (upper band / round-number confluence) or the 194 area (200 SMA, would confirm the reclaim) offer better reward/risk.
- **Bull case confirmation:** Sustained closes above ~203 on continued elevated volume would validate the breakout; the next measured resistance zones to watch are the 227.63 intraday high and, below that, the 215.98 gap-open level now acting as near-term support/resistance pivot.
- **Bear case trigger:** A close back below ~203, and especially below the 200 SMA at ~194, would mark the gap as a fade candidate with a gap-fill target toward ~183 (09-30 close).
- **Risk management:** With ATR at 9.58, a 2-ATR stop is ~19 points wide — position sizes should shrink accordingly, or use the 203/194 levels as tighter structural stops.

## Summary table

| Metric / Level | Value (2026-10-01) | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| Close | 212.30 | +15.8% vs prior close (183.37); event-driven gap |
| Intraday candle | Open 215.98 → Close 212.30, High 227.63, Low 211.04 | Fade from highs; sellers active above 220 |
| Volume | 28.98M | ~4–6x normal; confirms institutional repricing |
| 10 EMA | 186.64 | Price far above; strong short-term momentum |
| 50 SMA | 178.89 | Rising; price +18.7% above — extended |
| 200 SMA | 193.81 | Declining; price reclaimed it by ~9.5% |
| RSI | 70.01 | Overbought threshold; one-day jump from 52.3 |
| MACD / Signal / Hist | 2.57 / 1.81 / +0.76 | Fresh bullish crossover, single-bar driven |
| Bollinger UB / Mid / LB | 203.00 / 185.01 / 167.02 | Close above upper band; band expansion = volatility breakout |
| ATR | 9.58 | Up ~38% from ~7; widen stops or cut size |
| Key resistance | 215.98, 227.63 | Gap open, intraday high |
| Key support | 203.00, 193.81, 183.37 | Upper band, 200 SMA, gap-fill level |

**Bottom line:** ACN underwent a violent bullish repricing on 2026-10-01 that reclaims the 200-day trend benchmark and breaks out above the Bollinger envelope. The signal is bullish but immature — confirmation requires holding above ~203/194 in coming sessions. Elevated volatility (ATR 9.58) and an overbought RSI argue for staged entries on pullbacks rather than chasing strength.

# ACN Sentiment Report — 2026-09-24 to 2026-10-01

## 1. Source-by-source breakdown

User-tagged labels: **6 Bullish (27%) / 3 Bearish (14%) / 13 unlabeled (59%)**. A 2:1 bullish-to-bearish tagged ratio, but on a small sample and with most messages unlabeled.

The content of the unlabeled messages skews bullish-leaning, however. Dominant event: Accenture's fiscal Q4 print on Thursday 10-01 — revenue $18.7B (+6%, above the high end of guidance), EPS $3.29 — followed by a ~15–17% single-day surge (prints cited at +15.71% and +17% to ~$214), described as potentially the stock's best day on record. Options flow flagged $2.3M in Oct 16 $225 calls at 16.7x standing open interest (@PredictionFLO1), a speculative bullish tell. Sympathy/cross-read posts ($APP, $U, $NOW, $NKE) treat ACN's move as a sector-positive signal.

Bearish counter-signals exist but are thin and mostly short-term-trading oriented: 'easy short lol' (@lvztq), 'drop zone' (@permabull869), 'falling in power hour, all buyers bought' (@MrBuyHighSellLow), plus unlabeled profit-taking chatter ('dump dump dump', 'see ya at 200', 'who's selling????'). Notably, some late-session posts suggest intra-day fade concern — buyers questioning who was selling — a mild exhaustion signal after a record move.

## 2. Cross-source divergences and alignments

With two of three sources unavailable, true cross-source divergence cannot be measured. Within StockTwits alone there is a mild internal divergence: tagged sentiment (27%/14%) is more polarized than the dominant narrative, which is broadly celebratory about the earnings beat. No institutional news framing is available to confirm or challenge the retail read — itself a coverage gap worth flagging.

## 3. Dominant narrative themes

1. **Q4 earnings beat → record single-day rally.** Revenue/EPS above guidance and stronger new bookings reframed the 'AI will kill consulting' bear thesis — explicitly called out by @kevinbtravers.
2. **Hold vs. fade debate.** Multiple posts focus on whether the post-earnings bid survives; the verdict on 10-01 was that it held, with a minority expecting mean reversion ('easy short', 'drop zone', 'see ya at 200').
3. **Spillover/speculative positioning.** Call-buying flow and sympathy-ticker posts show traders treating the beat as a read-across for enterprise software/consulting peers.

## 4. Catalysts and risks

- **Catalyst (realized):** FY Q4 print on 10-01 — the single driver of essentially all observed sentiment.
- **Catalyst (forward):** Follow-through into the next sessions; the $225-strike call interest suggests traders are positioning for continuation toward $225–$250 ('$240 tomorrow', '$250 soon').
- **Risks:** Post-surge exhaustion/RSI 70 reading flagged by @PredictionFLO1; the 'all buyers bought' power-hour fade argument; a record one-day gain invites profit-taking. Missing news/Reddit coverage means the institutional and longer-horizon investor reaction is unmeasured — an important blind spot after a guidance-beating print.

## 5. Key sentiment signals

| Signal | Direction | Source | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q4 beat + record single-day rally | Bullish | StockTwits | +15.71%/+17% posts; revenue $18.7B above guidance; EPS $3.29 |
| Post-earnings bid holding | Bullish | StockTwits | 'relief held', 'holding way better than expected' |
| Tagged ratio 2:1 bullish | Mildly Bullish | StockTwits | 6 Bullish vs 3 Bearish of 22 msgs |
| Call buying Oct 16 $225 | Bullish (speculative) | StockTwits | $2.3M flow, 16.7x open interest |
| Late-day profit-taking / short interest | Bearish (minority) | StockTwits | 'easy short', 'drop zone', 'see ya at 200', 'all buyers bought' |
| RSI ~70 after surge | Caution | StockTwits | overbought flag in flow post |
| News & Reddit coverage | Silent | Yahoo/Reddit | both feeds unavailable — not absence of signal |

## Bottom line

Retail sentiment on ACN is mildly-to-moderately bullish, driven entirely by the 10-01 earnings beat and a record rally that held into the close. The bullish read is genuine but rests on one small, single-day social sample; with news and Reddit dark, confidence is **low**. The trader should treat this as a post-catalyst momentum signal with a live fade/mean-reversion debate, not a durable consensus.

# Accenture plc (ACN) — Fundamentals Report
Point-in-time: 2026-10-01 | All figures USD millions unless noted

## Data availability note
The fundamentals vendor withheld profile-level data (market cap, multiples, 52-week range, sector labels) for this date, and insider transaction data could not be served point-in-time (trades are dated by event, not filing date). This report is built entirely from SEC EDGAR-filed statements available as of 2026-10-01.

## Company profile (from filings)
Accenture plc is a global professional services company (consulting, technology, and managed services). It reports on a fiscal year ending August 31. The company is a large-cap, asset-light services business: it generates strong operating cash flow, runs modest capex, and returns most free cash to shareholders via buybacks and dividends (financing cash flow is persistently and heavily negative).

## Income statement — recent quarters (period ends)
- FY2025: Q1 (Nov 2024) rev 17,690 / NI 2,279 / EPS 3.59; Q2 (Feb 2025) rev 16,659 / NI 1,788 / EPS 2.82; Q3 (May 2025) rev 17,728 / NI 2,198 / EPS 3.49; Q4 (Aug 2025) rev 17,596 / NI 1,414 / EPS 2.25 (Q4 EPS dip — likely charges/seasonal margin trough, consistent with prior years' Aug-quarter softness in EPS vs revenue).
- FY2026 to date: Q1 (Nov 2025) rev 18,742 / op income 3,175 / NI 2,339 / EPS 3.80; Q2 (Feb 2026) rev 18,044 / op income 2,874 / NI 1,825 / EPS 2.93; Q3 (May 2026) rev 18,718 / op income 2,494 / NI 1,825 / EPS 2.93 (approx. per EPS line; Q3 NI per table 1,825 region).

Trends:
- Revenue growth has re-accelerated: FY26 quarters ran ~$18.0–18.7B vs ~$16.7–17.7B a year earlier — roughly +6–9% YoY, a marked pickup from the flat FY2023–2024 stretch (quarters hovering ~$15.8–16.5B).
- Operating margin is stable at ~13–17% of revenue depending on quarter (Q1 seasonally strongest). Q1 FY26 op margin ~16.9%.
- Diluted EPS continues compounding: TTM through May 2026 ≈ 3.80 + 2.93 + 2.93 + 2.25 ≈ ~$11.9/share, vs ~$10.9 a year earlier.
- Long arc: quarterly revenue roughly tripled from ~$5.5–6.5B (2009) to ~$18.7B (2026); EPS grew from ~$0.7 to ~$3.8 — consistent, low-drama compounding.

## Balance sheet
- Total assets $68.8B (May 2026), up steadily from ~$60B in late 2024 — partly acquisition-driven (investing outflows stepped up in FY2024–2025).
- Cash and equivalents $10.17B (May 2026), rebounding from ~$9.4B (Feb 2026) and ~$9.6B (Nov 2025). Cash has ranged $5–11.5B over the past five years.
- Stockholders' equity $31.9B and grinding upward each quarter (~$26.7B mid-2024 → ~$31.9B mid-2026).
- Current assets $28.9B vs current liabilities $21.6B → current ratio ~1.34, tight but typical for ACN; working capital position is stable and has been ~1.2–1.4x for years.
- Total liabilities line is not tagged by this filer, but assets minus equity implies ~$36.9B of liabilities + minority interests — dominated by operating liabilities (accrued comp, deferred revenue), not financial debt. Leverage is low.

## Cash flow
- Operating cash flow is strongly seasonal (Q2/Q4-weighted in the cumulative filing pattern). FY2026 nine months through May: $9.27B OCF vs $9.27B-equivalent prior-year 9M $9.27B (FY25 9M: $7.56B through May — wait, check: FY25 cumulative 9M = $7,560M; FY26 9M = $9,268M → +23% YoY). Strong cash conversion.
- Capex remains trivial: $492M for FY26 nine months (~1.5% of revenue) — classic asset-light profile. FCF ≈ $8.8B for 9M FY26.
- Financing outflow $7.1B over FY26 9M — buybacks + dividends continuing at a heavy pace; essentially all FCF is returned or reinvested via M&A.
- Investing outflow rose in FY2024–2025 (FY24: -$5.5B FY cumulative 9M; FY25 9M: -$3.45B; FY26 9M: -$3.45B) — acquisition spending remains elevated vs the ~$0.5–1.5B/yr norm pre-2021.

## Financial history context
- 2009–2019: steady mid-single-digit growth, EPS ~$0.4→~$2.0/quarter, equity built from ~$2.8B to ~$14B.
- 2020–2022: pandemic-era acceleration; quarterly revenue jumped from ~$11B to ~$16B.
- 2023–2024: growth stalled (~flat YoY quarters, some revenue declines) — the industry-wide discretionary consulting slowdown.
- 2025–2026: re-acceleration to ~$18B+ quarterly revenue, record OCF, record equity base. The business has exited the 2023–24 lull.

## Actionable insights for traders
1. Fundamental momentum is positive: revenue +6–9% YoY, EPS ~$11.9 TTM, 9M OCF +23% YoY. Dips that ignore this trajectory are not fundamentals-driven.
2. Watch the Aug-quarter pattern: Q4 (Aug) EPS has repeatedly come in soft relative to revenue (FY25 Q4 EPS 2.25 on $17.6B rev). Position sizing into the late-September/October earnings report should account for this seasonality.
3. Cash + buyback support: ~$10B cash and $7B+/yr of shareholder returns provide a persistent bid and per-share compounding even if organic growth flattens.
4. Low leverage, asset-light model = resilient to rate/credit shocks; the risk factors are demand-side (consulting budgets), not balance-sheet.
5. M&A spend is elevated (~$3.5B/yr investing outflow) — watch goodwill/intangible growth and integration commentary; assets growing faster than revenue is a yellow flag to monitor, not yet a red one.
6. Insider transactions: not available point-in-time for 2026-10-01 — no signal either way from insider activity in this dataset.

| Diluted EPS (TTM) | ~$11.9 | Rising from ~$10.9 | Steady compounding |
| Operating margin | ~13–17% qtrly | Stable | Q1 strongest seasonally |
| Operating cash flow (9M) | $9.27B | +23% YoY | Strong conversion |
| Capex (9M) | $0.49B | ~1.5% of rev | Asset-light |
| Financing outflow (9M) | -$7.1B | Persistent | Buybacks + dividends |
| Cash | $10.2B | Rebounding | Ample liquidity |
| Equity | $31.9B | Rising ~$1B/qtr | No dilution stress |
| Current ratio | ~1.34 | Stable | Normal for ACN |
| Debt | Minimal (liabilities mostly operating) | Low leverage | Resilient balance sheet |
| Insider activity | Data unavailable at 2026-10-01 | n/a | No signal |

Bottom line: ACN's fundamentals as of 2026-10-01 show a healthy, cash-generative compounder exiting the 2023–24 consulting slowdown — accelerating revenue, record cash flow, low leverage, and heavy shareholder returns. Fundamental bias: constructive; principal risks are demand cyclicality and M&A integration, not the balance sheet.

Bull Analyst: The bear hasn't even shown up yet, so let me set the table: ACN just delivered the single most decisive bullish signal we've seen all year, and it did so by demolishing the exact thesis the bears have been running on.

**The catalyst is fundamental, not technical froth.** Fiscal Q4 printed revenue of $18.7B — above the high end of guidance — with EPS of $3.29. This isn't a multiple-expansion story running ahead of reality; it's the market catching up to fundamentals that were already accelerating. Revenue has re-accelerated to +6–9% YoY after the 2023–24 consulting slowdown, TTM EPS is around $11.9 versus $10.9 a year ago, and nine-month operating cash flow is up 23% YoY to $9.3B on essentially zero capex (~1.5% of revenue). This is a cash compounder emerging from its trough, and the market just figured that out in one session.

**The "AI kills consulting" thesis is dead — and ACN killed it.** The bear case for the last two years has been that generative AI would commoditize consulting. What actually happened? Enterprises need someone to implement AI, and ACN is the largest beneficiary of enterprise AI-transformation budgets. The earnings print — with stronger new bookings — is direct, quantified evidence that AI demand is flowing *to* Accenture, not around it. The sector confirms it: peers EPAM, DXC, EXL all traded up the same week. This is a sector-wide repricing of IT services as AI-implementers, and ACN is the bellwether with the biggest moat: global scale, C-suite relationships, and an asset-light model that converts growth straight into free cash.

**The tape confirms institutional conviction.** Yes, RSI hit 70 and the stock closed above the upper Bollinger band — the bear will call that overbought. But look at the character of the move: 28.98M shares, roughly 4–6x normal volume, and critically, the bid *held* into the close. Social flow noted "the relief held... the bid survived the 8 AM call" and a $2.3M sweep into October $225 calls at 16.7x open interest — traders aren't fading this, they're positioning for continuation toward $225–250. A gap that holds on record volume after a guidance-beating print is repricing, not exhaustion. Exhaustion gaps fade the next day; this one absorbed sellers all session.

**Pre-empting the bear's best arguments:**

- *"It's extended, wait for the pullback."* Fair — and the bull case doesn't require chasing at 212. Holding above ~203 (upper band) and ~194 (the reclaimed 200 SMA) confirms the breakout; pullbacks to those levels are entry points, not thesis breaks. What matters is ACN decisively reclaimed the 200-day after trading below it all window. That changes the regime.
- *"Q4 EPS is seasonally soft."* Historically true (FY25 Q4 EPS $2.25) — which makes this quarter's beat-and-hold even more impressive. The seasonal trough just produced a record rally.
- *"Macro is fragile — Gundlach's 'hollow tree.'"* ACN is exactly where capital rotates in a fragile tape: low leverage, ~$10B cash, $7B+/yr returned to shareholders, a persistent buyback bid under the stock. It's the defensive quality name within tech services.
- *"The death cross still exists."* The 50/200 spread is narrowing with price now ~9.5% above the 200 SMA. If ACN holds these levels, the golden-cross setup becomes a real medium-term tailwind — the gap didn't just move price, it repaired the entire trend structure.

**The bottom line:** ACN combines accelerating fundamentals (+6–9% revenue, +23% OCF, ~$11.9 TTM EPS), a validated AI-services demand story, a fortress balance sheet with a built-in buyback bid, and a technical regime shift confirmed by record volume. The risks — post-surge consolidation and M&A integration drift — are timing risks, not thesis risks. Staged entries on pullbacks toward 203/194 with structural stops below the 200 SMA give bulls a defined-risk way to own the sector's strongest compounder at the moment its narrative inflected.
bear_history:
Bear Analyst: Let me start where the bull just admitted the whole problem without realizing it: they spent their entire opening pre-empting bear arguments instead of making new bullish ones. That's what you do when you know the entry price is the weakest part of your case.

**The tape the bull is celebrating is actually a textbook fade setup.** Strip away the narrative and look at 10-01 dispassionately: opened at 215.98, hit 227.63, closed at 212.30. That is a candle that opened above where it closed, gave back 15 points from the high, and closed near the bottom of a 16.6-point range — on 4–6x volume. The bull calls this "absorbing sellers." I'd call it something else: the largest volume day in months was used by informed holders to distribute into retail euphoria. When a stock prints a record rally and *still* finishes well off its highs, the smart money wasn't buying the close — they were selling your open. The social feed itself flagged it: "falling in power hour, all buyers bought." That's not a bullish tell, that's an exhaustion tell.

**The "overbought" dismissal deserves more respect than the bull gave it.** RSI went from 52 to 70 in one session. The close is 18.7% above the 50-day and above an upper Bollinger band that itself just exploded from ~196 to 203. Single-bar repricings like this have a well-documented behavior: they mean-revert toward the gap zone. The bull's own trade plan concedes this — "staged entries at 203/194." Think about what that admission means: the bull is telling you the right price is 5–9% lower than the current price. If the best bullish advice is "wait for 203 or 194," then buying at 212 is paying the gap-chaser's tax. And if 194 fails? The gap-fill target is 183 — right back where it started, a -14% round trip.

**Now the fundamentals, where the bull's "acceleration" story is thinner than advertised.** Yes, revenue grew +6–9%. But look at what the market just paid for it: ~17.8% overnight for a services company growing high single digits. Let's do the math nobody at the celebration wants to do — TTM EPS ~$11.9, price $212 → you're paying roughly 18x trailing earnings for a business whose multi-decade compounding rate is mid-to-high single digits, and whose FY26 quarterly EPS actually shows a *declining* trend through the year: 3.80 → 2.93 → 2.93, with Q4 seasonally soft. Operating income went 3,175 → 2,874 → 2,494 across FY26 — margins *compressed* each quarter even as revenue grew. The bull says "acceleration"; the income statement says decelerating profitability on accelerating revenue. That's the profile of a company buying growth with pricing concessions — consistent with an AI-services land grab where ACN wins volume but gives up margin.

**The "AI killed the bear thesis" claim is premature victory.** One quarter of bookings strength doesn't resolve a structural question. The actual bear thesis was never "AI makes consulting disappear" — it's that AI *deflates the billable-hour pyramid* over time, forcing pricing model transitions and compressing the very margins we just watched compress for three straight quarters. Q4 revenue at the "high end of guidance" is a company being good at guiding, not proof of structural AI tailwinds. And the peer rally the bull cites — EPAM, DXC up — happened in the same news vacuum where we couldn't verify a single ACN-specific headline. Sympathy moves are the weakest kind of corroboration.

**The macro and data-quality caveats are doing real work here.** Gundlach's "hollow tree" warning arrives in a tape where a 17% single-day gap in a mega-cap services name is exactly the kind of late-cycle exuberance that precedes mean reversion. The bull says ACN is "defensive" in a risk-off — defensives still draw down, they just draw down less, and nothing about a stock trading 18.7% above its 50-day is defensive *at this price*. Meanwhile, our sentiment sample is one day of StockTwits posts, the news feed is dark, FRED is unconfigured, and insider data is unavailable. The bull built a "regime change" thesis on the thinnest evidentiary window possible.

**The death cross point deserves a rebuttal too.** The bull claims the gap "repaired the trend structure." It did nothing of the kind — it repaired *price*. The 50 SMA (178.89) still sits below the 200 SMA (193.81), and the 200 is still declining. A gap doesn't fix a moving average; only time above it does. If price chops sideways here — the base case after a volatility breakout with ATR at 9.58 — the gap's mechanical effect on the averages fades and you're left holding a stock that spent weeks below a falling 200-day.

**Where I actually agree with the bull:** this is a good company. Fortress balance sheet, $10B cash, ~$9B of annual FCF, a persistent buyback. But "good company" and "good entry at $212 after a record gap" are different statements, and conflating them is the oldest mistake in the book. Every risk-management signal in the technical report — overbought RSI, close above the band, ATR +38%, bearish intraday candle, "all buyers bought" power-hour chatter — says the same thing: the first buyers of this gap are the liquidity for the second leg, not the beneficiaries of it.

**My case:** Let it prove 203 holds. If it does, fine — you paid a premium for confirmation. If it doesn't, you're looking at 194, and below that, a gap-fill to 183 that would turn this "decisive bullish signal" into the year's most expensive fake-out. The bull needs ACN to do something it has never done before — sustain a record single-day repricing without retracing — while I just need gravity to work.
